claims: A snow squall is a sudden, intense burst of moderate-to-heavy snow.
Snow squalls are accompanied by strong, gusty surface winds.
Snow squalls result in whiteout conditions (near-zero visibility).
Snow squalls typically last 30 to 60 minutes.
Snow squalls rarely last more than an hour or two.
Snow squalls cause rapid temperature drops.
Snow squalls often turn a sunny day into a whiteout within minutes.
Snow squalls cause flash-freezing of roads.
Snow squalls lead to multi-car accidents.
Snow squalls involve vertical air movement.
A blizzard features heavy snow and high winds lasting for several hours or more.
The National Weather Service issues Snow Squall Warnings.
Snow squalls can cause rapid pileups.
